MARKET.head: Federal ban on hemp THC drinks takes effect November 2026, upending state markets
MARKET.summ: Until recently, there was no federal guidance on the sale and consumption of hemp-derived THC-infused beverages, leading to a confusing, state-by-state patchwork of regulations
takeaways: Congress passed legislation in November 2025 capping THC at 0.4 milligrams per container, effective November 12, 2026, banning most hemp-derived THC beverages nationally.
Hemp THC-infused drink sales hit $239 million in the 52 weeks prior to April 2026, with the potential market valued at $9.9 to $14.9 billion.
Art Nergaryan's Massachusetts wine and cheese shops saw revenue jump 25 to 35 percent after stocking THC drinks, but state regulators banned their sale in wine stores in May 2024.
State regulations remain inconsistent: Minnesota and Georgia permit hemp beverages, while California, Washington and Vermont restrict or ban them outside cannabis-licensed retail.
Diana Eberlein, chair of the Coalition for Adult Beverage Alternatives, says the patchwork of state rules without federal clarity has blocked industry growth and legitimacy.

MARKET.head: Albanian wine industry emerges after 30 years of isolation
MARKET.summ: One of the oldest wine-producing regions in the world, Albania is in the midst of a quality revolution as vignerons embrace native grape varieties
takeaways: Albania produced 3.03 million liters of wine in 2022 and exported $560,000 in 2024, mostly to Europe, with sporadic US sales in Texas and Michigan.
Grape production jumped over 250 percent between 2000 and 2016 as producers trained in Italy, Greece, France, and Germany returned with new winemaking techniques.
The country has no official geographically designated regions but grows distinct styles across northern, central, and southern zones shaped by elevation, soil, and climate.
Indigenous grapes including Kallmet, Shesh, Debina, Pulës, and Vlosh are gaining prominence alongside international varieties as producers adopt small-scale and minimal-intervention methods.
Tourism and consumer education campaigns frame Albanian wines as Mediterranean or continental expressions, positioning the nation for broader global recognition over the next 10-20 years.

MARKET.head: English estates launch prestige cuvées at Champagne prices
MARKET.summ: Are English prestige cuvées worth prices that rival the top end of Champagne?
takeaways: Nyetimber released England's first prestige cuvée, the 1086 range, in 2018 at £150, £175, priced on par with premium Champagne and aged seven years minimum on lees.
Chapel Down's Kit's Coty Coeur de Cuvée (2017, £126) and Gusbourne's Fifty One Degrees North (2022, £195) followed, establishing super-premium English sparkling as a recognised category.
Langham Winery's Tommy Grimshaw created an innovative multi-vintage solera-aged Perpetual Blanc de Blancs (2025, £109.95), inspired by grower Champagne pioneer Anselme Selosse.
Squerryes launched prestige cuvée Patience 2014 in July 2026, completing a lineup of five estates positioning English sparkling wines as luxury products commanding £100 and above.
These bottlings are released in small quantities, often from exceptional vintages, with extended ageing and specific vineyard provenance mirroring Champagne's prestige cuvée model.

MARKET.head: Centre-Loire neighbours offer Sancerre quality at half the price
MARKET.summ: Those interested in French wine are undoubtedly familiar with the Loire Valley, but digging a little deeper, there are many subregions within this expansive viticultural area to get to know. One of them is the Centre-Loire. And although the slightly misleading name suggests it’s the center of France’s lengthy and endlessly...
takeaways: Sancerre Sauvignon Blanc now sells for $40, $50, straining buyer budgets as the appellation reaches production capacity with no plans to expand.

Five neighbouring Centre-Loire appellations, Pouilly-Fumé, Menetou-Salon, Quincy, Reuilly, and Coteaux du Giennois, produce similar Sauvignon Blancs at $20, $30, gaining market traction as Sancerre prices rise.
Clément Berthier, Sancerre appellation president, notes the region is smaller than its global reputation; nearly three-quarters of Sancerre goes to export, half to the United States.
Pinot Noir from Centre-Loire is improving in quality and price relative to Burgundy, with winemakers including Matthieu Delaporte at Domaine Delaporte positioning it as an alternative.

Earlier harvests driven by climate change threaten acidity; winemakers including Emile Balland and Paul-Henry Pellé of Domaine Pellé in Menetou-Salon are experimenting with abandoned varieties blended at 5–10 percent to retain freshness.

MARKET.head: World Cup failed to reverse beer's steepening US sales decline.
MARKET.summ: Long before the World Cup first kicked off earlier this summer, Wall Street analysts, industry insiders, and rank-and-file bar owners were already anxiously talking up the potential sales boost it might bring the beleaguered beer business. All those games, all those fans, all those “occasions”… it would have to add up to something, right?
takeaways: Anheuser-Busch InBev spent $110 million on global Michelob Ultra campaigns tied to the 2026 World Cup, projecting only 0.25 percent annual volume lift from the effort.
US beer category sales fell 2.1 percent in dollars and 3.4 percent in volume year-over-year in the final week of the tournament, accelerating prior declines.
On-premise draft sales rose 7.1 percent in dollars during the tournament across BeerBoard's bar network, but declined in the final week as the event ended.
Off-premise scan data tracked by Circana showed ABI's portfolio down 0.7 percent in dollars and 2.3 percent in volume through mid-July.
Spirits outperformed beer significantly, with Cutwater spirits up 60 percent in dollars and volume in the tournament's final week.

CULTURE.head: Young wine workers reshape how their peers discover wine
CULTURE.summ: To help spread the word that wine is for everyone, we ask Zoomers working in the wine industry - bars, restaurants, cellars and retail - to share their experience of a bottle they love
takeaways: Daria Volokitina, sommelier at Hotel Plaza Athénée in Paris, paired Austrian Furmint with casual barbecue to show wine works beyond formal dining and traditional food pairings.
Alex Padilla, retail staff at Hi-Time Wine Cellars in Costa Mesa, California, uses social media and store interactions to position wine as accessible to younger drinkers skeptical of the category.
Both sommeliers say their generation sees wine as no longer reserved for those who 'understand' it or confined to fine dining, shifting it toward everyday occasions.
Young industry workers believe simply being visible young faces in wine retail and hospitality helps counteract perception that wine excludes younger drinkers.
Natural wines and value-driven Californian reds appeal to this cohort, though many younger consumers still lack basic knowledge of wine styles and categories.

CULTURE.head: Ancient vine-training systems vanish as labor costs and mechanization reshape European viticulture
CULTURE.summ: As labor costs soar, global wine regions are forced to weigh the high expense of traditional vineyard design against its tourism appeal and climate-adapting benefits
takeaways: Italy's alberata system, depicted in 1793 Naples landscapes with vines draped across poplar and elm trees, has shrunk to only a handful of hectares as mechanizable methods like Guyot replaced it by the late 20th century.

Familia Torres maintains pergola training at Pazo Torre Panelas in Rías Baixas, Spain, using adapted machinery for ground work; the DO's harvest ban on mechanization means all training systems demand equal manual labor at picking.

The bellussera hybrid system in Veneto's Piave DOC, once supporting silk production and livestock fodder, now covers nine percent of the region but may gain viability from climate resilience and wine tourism as erratic weather intensifies.

CULTURE.head: NYC housing complex opens pathways built from 450,000 recycled wine corks
CULTURE.summ: Wine bottle corks are getting a second lease on life in New York City. Earlier this month, a New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) project in Brooklyn cut the ribbon on newly paved pathways and playground surfaces made of upcycled corks. The first-of-its-kind installation is part of the nonprofit Public Housing Community...
takeaways: Public Housing Community Fund partnered with Cork Collective, Rockwell Group, and Amorim to build playgrounds and walkways from recycled corks at Marlboro Houses in Brooklyn.
Cork Collective sourced over 450,000 corks from NYC restaurants, ground them in Wisconsin, mixed with adhesive, and installed the surfaces at the NYCHA complex.
Children at Marlboro Houses submitted playground designs that Center for Justice Innovation, The Urban Conga, and the Resident Association incorporated into the final layout.
Cork surfaces absorb stormwater, reduce heat by 20 to 30 percent, and offer non-toxic alternatives to plastic or asphalt while diverting waste from landfills.
Globally, 13 billion corks are made yearly but less than one percent recycled; 3 billion corks are discarded in the US annually.

SCIENCE.head: Pierce's Disease Threat Expands Across Europe as Climate Warms
SCIENCE.summ: As warming temperatures increase the risk of Pierce’s disease in European vineyards, researchers and growers are looking to California for lessons in detection, prevention, and management
takeaways: Pierce's disease, caused by the bacterium Xylella fastidiosa, devastated California's wine industry from the late 1990s onward, costing growers over $48 million annually and killing large vineyard blocks.
The disease was detected in European grapevines on Spain's Mallorca island in 2016 and in continental Europe in Portugal in 2023, with cases now confirmed in Spain, Italy, Portugal, and France.

A 2025 climate study found 41.2 percent of European vineyards face climate risk, up from 21.8 percent in previous models, with riverside and valley microclimates especially vulnerable as winters warm.
California's decades of experience show early detection, vector management, and rapid diagnostics can slow spread once the disease becomes established, though eradication requires swift action.

European growers and regulators lack unified communication strategies and mandatory reporting systems, risking delayed detection and potential concealment of infections if vine destruction remains the only solution.

SCIENCE.head: How light exposure and soil control green pepper aromas in wine grapes
SCIENCE.summ: Understanding the divisive aroma compounds best known for creating green notes like bell pepper and grass in Bordeaux grapes
takeaways: Methoxypyrazines, nitrogen-based compounds causing bell pepper and grassiness, accumulate early in berry development then decline sharply at veraison in varieties like Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc.

Light exposure on grape clusters is the primary factor controlling pyrazine concentration; shoot removal and leaf plucking reduce shade and lower these aromas, research from Dominique Roujou de Boubee's 1995 University of Bordeaux study showed.

Soil type affects pyrazines indirectly through vine vigor: gravel soils with low water retention produce lower pyrazine grapes, while limestone and clay-silt soils encourage vegetative growth and higher concentrations in Cabernet Sauvignon.
Rootstock choice influences pyrazine levels in both grapes and stems by altering canopy vigor, though Dr David Jeffery of University of Adelaide notes genetic effects of rootstock remain unresolved.

Temperature appears to correlate with lower pyrazine intensity, but the mechanism remains unclear; winemaker Duncan Meyers of Arnot-Roberts in Napa observes cooler vintages and cooler sites consistently show higher pyrazine expression.

SCIENCE.head: Disease-resistant hybrid grapes cut fungicide spraying by up to 80 percent
SCIENCE.summ: Fungus-resistant hybrid grape varieties, known as PIWIs, are evolving through advances in breeding, offering growers new options in a changing climate
takeaways: PIWI grapes, bred to resist powdery and downy mildew, require two to three fungicide sprays per season versus eight to 15 for traditional varieties like Cabernet Franc.
Genetic technology rhAmpSeq, deployed since 2019 under the US VitisGen initiative, allows breeders to identify disease-resistance genes with precision and stack multiple protections into new hybrids.
Modern PIWIs now contain up to 95 percent Vitis vinifera genetic material through backcrossing, retaining traditional wine quality while inheriting American vine fungal resistance.
A 2026 Luxembourg study showed PIWIs delivered twofold economic savings and threefold environmental benefit versus traditional varieties, with gains in soil ecology and reduced water toxicity.
Germany leads adoption with 4,000 hectares of PIWI vines in 2025; Bordeaux and Swiss breeders are developing regionally-adapted hybrids including ResDur crosses with Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot.

SCIENCE.head: Vineyards deploy shade netting to cool clusters and preserve phenolics in heat
SCIENCE.summ: Netting is no longer just for hail, it is becoming one of viticulture's most versatile climate adaptation tools
takeaways: UC Davis found that shaded Cabernet clusters at Oakville had 27 percent more anthocyanins than unshaded fruit when temperatures exceeded 35 degrees Celsius, the threshold for pigment degradation.

Luis Reginato, viticulture head at Catena Zapata in Mendoza, uses light netting and canopy management to deliver filtered sunlight in brief pulses rather than sustained direct exposure to prevent heat stress.

Marco Simonit's 2025 trials at Petra in Tuscany showed that shade netting reduced Merlot cluster temperature from 50 to 40-41 degrees Celsius and cut sunburn incidence from 41 percent to three percent.
White and green nets outperformed black nets in trials, absorbing less heat; nets must be positioned away from clusters to prevent the heated fabric itself from burning fruit.
Achille Boroli at Boroli estate in Barolo uses one-sided netting on south-facing slopes to cool clusters without trapping heat, reducing hours above 35 degrees Celsius from 210 to far fewer annually.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The taste of stone
NEWSLETTERS.summ: You need more than an excavator to create a Grand Cru vineyard, but it definitely helps
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Jako Andabak purchased an ailing cooperative in Bol, Brač island in 2009, founding Stina winery and modernizing it with new vineyards.
Stina's early wines, debuted at Zagreb Wine Gourmet Weekend in April 2012, signaled a new wave of well-capitalized Croatian producers called 'Hrvatski Vrh.'.
Andabak leveraged his existing hotel business on Brač to provide capital and ready market for Stina's wines.
Croatian EU ascension in 2013 motivated new winery projects to establish themselves before Brussels agricultural regulations took effect.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Four wines from Virginia in the USA
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I tried these four wines from Virginia in the USA. It’s a state that is quite challenging for viticulture, with
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Virginia has 300 wineries and 1,600 hectares of vineyards, with 75% Vitis vinifera and 25% hybrids, despite challenging hot humid summers.
Rosemont of Virginia's Kilravock 2023 (44% Merlot, 28% Cabernet Franc, 28% Petit Verdot) aged 18 months in French and American oak scored 93/100.
Southwest Mountains Vineyards SMV Merlot 2023 from Monticello scored 93/100 for its smooth black cherry and blackberry fruit with soft tannins.
Barboursville Cabernet Franc Reserve 2023 with 10% Petit Verdot scored 92/100 and costs $25 USD.
Domaine Finot's Turk Mountain Petit Verdot 2023 used whole cluster fermentation with wild yeasts and no added sulfites, scoring 93/100 but developing mousiness by day two.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Vinography Images: Under African Skies
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Dramatic skies make for a beautiful evening above vineyards near Stellenbosch, South Africa. Known traditionally as the home of South
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Who's Afraid of Volatile Wines?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The wine industry's obsession with protecting you from acetic acid
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: EU law limits volatile acidity to 1.2 g/L in red wines; Loire vigneron Sébastien David was ordered to destroy 2,000+ bottles of Cabernet Franc exceeding this limit in 2019.
The EU's current 1.2 g/L volatile acidity limit originated in 1979 and lacks clear scientific justification; vinegar requires 40 g/L to form, and 10% concentration is needed for health concern.
The US permits 1.4 g/L volatile acidity in red wines, rising to 1.7 g/L for super-ripe grapes; EU exceptions now allow up to 2.4 g/L in 18 countries' hundreds of appellations.
Orange wines must meet the white wine volatile acidity limit of 1.08 g/L despite having tannin and VA levels similar to reds, creating regulatory inconsistency.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Michelin And The Death Of The Wine Guide
NEWSLETTERS.summ: It was entirely predictable that Michelin’s new venture into wine would trigger huffy French recriminations. Its Wine Selection Burgundy 2026, launched this month, awarded nine producers the top accolade of three grapes, another 20 vignerons two grapes, and 33 one grape. A further 32 were merely “selected”.
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Michelin's Wine Selection Burgundy 2026 awarded nine producers three grapes, 20 vignerons two grapes, 33 one grape, and 32 were 'selected.'.
Domaine Arnoux-Lachaux publicly demanded removal from Michelin's guide after receiving only one grape despite being a celebrated Vosne-Romanée house.
Michelin rates producers based on vineyard management and consistency rather than individual wines, unlike competitor Guide Hachette des Vins which rates specific cuvées.
Michelin acquired Wine Advocate entirely in 2019 after purchasing 40% in 2017, raising questions about whether WA Editor-in-Chief William Kelley influenced selections.

Consumer wine guides emerged in the 1970s with Decanter, Wine Spectator, and Hugh Johnson's Pocket Wine Book, but the internet and expansion of global wine variety have rendered comprehensive print guides obsolete.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Notable Releases from Troon Vineyard
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Notes on a Vermentino and two Syrahs, one with some bottle age
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Troon Vineyard released 2025 Vermentino and 2023 Syrah from Oregon's Applegate Valley.
Troon Vineyard, located in Grant's Pass, farms with certified biodynamic and regenerative organic practices.
Troon uses only ambient cultures for fermentation, minimal sulfite at bottling, and ages wine in neutral vessels instead of new oak.
Applegate Valley's alluvial soils and overnight temperature drops from Siskiyou Mountains create ideal conditions for Mediterranean grape varieties.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Q&8 | Wang Yuanzhu Talks Grapes, Grain & Ancient Wine
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Coram Collective 集岩酿造 ranks among the most intriguing projects to pop up in China in recent years. Founded in 2023, with production from 2024, this
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: Coram Collective, founded in 2023 with production from 2024, co-ferments rice wine with grape varieties like Chardonnay and Merlot, and innovates huangjiu (yellow wine).
Co-founder Alex Yuanzhu Wang was inspired by a Burgundy winemaker's optimism about Chinese wine and huangjiu, leading her to build a ricery in Shaoxing.
Coram's products are already listed in over 100 bars and restaurants across Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, Guangzhou and Chengdu since launching last June.
Best huangjiu typically shows its quality between three and eight years of aging; most loses freshness after 10 years, contradicting assumptions that older is better.
Chardomi blends 80% Chardonnay grapes with 20% glutinous rice through a multi-step process: rice saccharification, wild yeast fermentation, then co-fermentation with pressed grape juice.

NEWSLETTERS.head: What I Learned at a Conference on Drinking
NEWSLETTERS.summ: From the invention of moderation to the return of temperance
NEWSLETTERS.author: Felicity Carter
takeaways: Drinking studies treats alcohol as cultural and social practice rather than a drink or health hazard, an interdisciplinary field that includes historians, anthropologists, sociologists, and other academics.

Researching drinking history is extremely difficult because drinking was so ubiquitous that ordinary people's habits were rarely documented; historical records focus on aberrant behavior or aristocrats.

Ireland's 2018 Public Health (Alcohol) Act introduced minimum unit pricing, supermarket barriers, advertising restrictions, and cancer warning labels; labels were pushed back to September 2028 from May 2026.
Spain and Italy challenged Ireland's cancer warning labels on alcohol via EU and WTO, not Big Alcohol as claimed; they opposed labels on valued cultural products.
The Industrial Revolution shifted the meaning of moderation from avoiding disgraceful drunkenness to maintaining worker sobriety, reliability and punctuality tied to economic productivity.
